title: Talent Shadowing and Role Handback Protocol
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:
This playbook defines Redwood's formal Talent Shadowing and Role Handback Protocol: the structured process for pairing incoming hires, role transitions, and temporary covers with existing owners to accelerate competency, minimize single-point-of-failure risk, and create auditable handback artifacts for future hires. It ties hiring intake, onboarding sprints, manager responsibilities, and performance feedback into a single, repeatable flow.

Why this exists:
- Reduce time-to-autonomy by providing focused observational and active practice windows.
- Ensure role knowledge is documented and demonstrable before handback.
- Standardize manager responsibilities and acceptance criteria for role transfer.
- Provide an evidence trail for performance conversations and post-hire retrospectives.

Scope:
- Applies to: new hires (full-time, contractors with >12 week engagements), role lateral transfers, interim cover assignments, and rotational apprenticeship programs.
- Not intended for: one-off shadowing for interview prep or informal buddy-check-ins (those are encouraged but out of scope).

Roles and responsibilities:
- Hiring Manager: owns the Shadow Plan, acceptance criteria, and final handback sign-off.
- Shadow Buddy (Current Owner): provides day-to-day mentoring, creates artifacts, assigns exercises, and documents gaps.
- Shadowing Participant (Incoming/Transferring Individual): completes exercises, documents questions, and demonstrates competency against the rubric.
- People Ops (Enablement): provides templates, coordinates logistics, ensures documentation is preserved in the knowledge repo and triggers checkpoint reminders.
- Team Lead / Tech Lead: validates technical artifacts and approves the participant's technical demo.
- Security/Compliance SME (when required): signs off on access and sensitive process handoffs.

Shadowing modalities (choose one or mix):
- Observe-Only: passive observation of meetings, tickets, and triage for the first week.
- Paired-Do: participant acts with buddy over live tasks with buddy oversight.
- Reverse Teach: participant prepares a micro-training and teaches the team feature/process to verify understanding.
- Ownership Sprint: time-boxed responsibility (24–72 hours) where participant owns low-risk operations under on-call-style escalation.

High-level timeline (recommended):
1) Pre-start (Hiring / Offer accepted)
   - Manager creates Shadow Plan (template below) and shares with People Ops and buddy.
   - Access checklist initiated (minimum required access granted by day 0; any privileged access requests must be submitted to Security SME).
2) Day 0–7: Orientation + Observe-Only
   - Participant completes orientation modules and 3 observation checkpoints (meetings, triage, code review).
   - Manager & buddy review initial questions and adjust plan.
3) Week 2–4: Paired-Do + Exercises
   - Participant completes 6 assigned exercises (mix of tickets and infrastructure run-throughs).
   - Weekly feedback checkpoint recorded in evidence portfolio.
4) Week 4–8: Ownership Sprint + Reverse Teach
   - Participant runs an Ownership Sprint for an agreed scope and presents a 20–30 minute Reverse Teach.
   - Tech Lead completes technical validation checklist.
5) Handback Sign-off (no later than week 8 for standard hires)
   - Manager collects artifacts, completes the acceptance rubric, and signs off in the protocol record.
   - People Ops archives artifacts in /knowledge-repo/team/<team-name>/handoffs/.

Acceptance criteria (manager signoff required):
- Functional: participant completed all required exercises and Ownership Sprint without critical errors (no unresolved P1/P0 incidents caused during sprint).
- Technical: tech lead verified code/config changes and the participant completed required PRs or infra changes.
- Documentation: role playbook, runbooks, run commands, and incident run-through notes are updated and linked.
- Security: least-privilege access confirmed, any secrets rotation or KMS handover completed.
- Feedback: manager and buddy feedback ratings at or above threshold (see rubric).

Feedback and performance rubric (use 1–5 scale; 1 = needs support, 5 = independent):
- Domain Knowledge: 1–5
- Execution: 1–5
- Troubleshooting & Debugging: 1–5
- Documentation Quality: 1–5
- Communication & Handoff Clarity: 1–5
- Composite threshold for signoff: average >= 3.8 and no dimension <= 2.

Artifacts to produce (must be links or attachments in the handback record):
- Shadow Plan (template).
- Evidence portfolio: list of tickets/PRs, screenshots of completed tasks, meeting notes.
- Ownership Sprint report (inc. steps, outcomes, issues, remediation).
- Reverse Teach slides/recording.
- Updated role playbook / runbooks (include diff or commit link).
- Access checklist confirmation signed by Security SME if privileged access was granted.

Sample Shadow Plan template (table):
| Item | Owner | Due | Acceptance Criteria | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Orientation checklist | People Ops | Day 0 | 100% completed | links to modules |
| Observation 3 meetings | Buddy | Day 5 | Participant recorded 3 takeaways | meeting links |
| 6 exercises | Buddy/Manager | Week 2–4 | PRs merged / tickets closed | include ticket IDs |
| Ownership Sprint | Participant | Week 4–8 | No P1 caused; ticket throughput documented | scope: infra read-only |

Manager checklist before signoff (numbered procedure):
1. Confirm all artifacts are uploaded to the handback record.
2. Verify feedback rubric averages meet threshold and discuss any low scores with participant.
3. Ensure tech lead and security SME have signed off where required.
4. Execute a 30-minute live knowledge demo with the participant in an all-hands or team forum and record it.
5. Mark the handback record as 'completed' and notify People Ops to archive.

Escalation and rollback policy:
- If during an Ownership Sprint the participant causes a P1/P0 incident, the buddy/manager executes 'ownership rollback':
  1) Remove participant write access to the system within 30 minutes.
  2) Buddy/manager takes ownership of incident remediation.
  3) People Ops schedules a 1:1 coaching and a revised shadow plan with extended paired-do windows.
  4) Re-assessment occurs after the revised plan (no earlier than 2 weeks).

Measuring success (OKRs / KPIs):
- Median time-to-first-merged-PR: target <= 14 days for backend/infra roles, <= 10 for frontend/docs.
- Median time-to-independent-sla-ownership: target <= 45 days.
- Shadow artifact coverage: 95% of role checklist items have an associated artifact.
- Manager satisfaction score (post-handback survey): target >= 4.2 / 5.

Special cases and adaptations:
- Senior hires: compress timeline to 2–4 weeks; require Reverse Teach focused on architecture decisions.
- Contractors <12 weeks: use an accelerated 2-week Ownership Sprint and restrict privileged access.
- Distributed teams / different timezones: schedule overlapping paired windows and require written asynchronous notes for every session.

FAQs:
Q: Who decides which tasks are safe for Ownership Sprints?
A: Manager + Buddy + Tech Lead agree and list safe scopes in the Shadow Plan before the sprint.

Q: What if the buddy leaves mid-shadowing?
A: Manager assigns an interim buddy within 48 hours and extends the shadow window by at least one week. All artifacts must be re-reviewed by the new buddy.

Q: Can a participant request an extension?
A: Yes. Extensions are documented and require manager approval and a revised plan; People Ops tracks extensions for trend analysis.

Operational notes for People Ops enablement:
- Trigger automated reminders at Day 7, Day 21, Day 42.
- Verify artifacts are saved under the canonical path: /knowledge-repo/team/<team-name>/handoffs/<hire-id>-<date>/
- Maintain a quarterly sample audit of 10% of handbacks for completeness and quality.

Appendix: Quick command checklist examples (for infra-facing roles)
- Validate access: aws sts get-caller-identity --profile <participant>
- Validate infra read-only: terraform plan -no-color -input=false
- Incident replay doc template: incident-replay-YYYYMMDD.md

Document ownership and review cadence:
- Owner: People Ops (Aisha Patel).
- Reviewers: People Ops, Eng Managers, Security SME.
- Review cadence: annually or after any incident involving a failed handback.
